title: Reasoning models and test-time compute
summary: A reasoning model spends extra hidden tokens thinking before it answers, and a per-request effort setting decides how many. More thinking costs time and money and only helps when the task is hard enough to use it.
useIf: The task needs multi-step planning, debugging or analysis and you can measure whether more thinking improves the result.
avoidIf: The task is lookup, classification, extraction or voice, where latency and output-token cost matter more than depth.

explain.md: A **reasoning model** produces hidden reasoning tokens before the visible answer. Those tokens are billed as output tokens and count against the output cap. **Test-time compute** is the general idea: spend more computation per answer instead of only at training time. Snell et al. (2024-08) found that allocating test-time compute by prompt difficulty improved efficiency by more than 4x over best-of-N, and that a smaller model with non-trivial success on a problem could beat a 14x larger one in a FLOPs-matched comparison [[r6]]. The s1 paper (2025-01) shows **budget forcing**: cut thinking short, or append `Wait` to extend it. Extending raised AIME24 from 50% to 57% [[r7]]. The lesson is that returns depend on difficulty. Easy prompts gain little.

explain.title: Output headroom

vars.v: the cap, shared by hidden reasoning and the visible answer

explain.example: OpenAI advises reserving at least **25,000** tokens for reasoning plus output when you start. Hitting the cap gives `status: incomplete`, which can happen before any visible text [[r1]].

explain.md: Treat effort as a **cost and latency dial**, not only a quality dial. Start at the vendor default, raise it only when an eval shows a gain, and lower it for voice, classification and retrieval. OpenAI advises giving reasoning models a clear goal, constraints and an output contract instead of scripting every intermediate step [[r1]]. In tool loops on the Responses API, pass reasoning items back with function outputs. In stateless mode (`store` false or ZDR) they carry `encrypted_content` by default [[r1]].

whereToUse: Multi-step coding, debugging and migration work where tests can confirm the result
Planning steps inside an agent, where a wrong plan wastes many later calls
Escalation paths: a cheap first pass, then a high-effort retry only for failures

use: The task is hard enough that a standard model fails the eval
Quality gains from effort are measured, not assumed
A background or batch path tolerates the extra latency
avoid: Interactive or voice paths with a tight time-to-first-token budget
Routine lookups, classification and extraction that a standard model already gets right
You have no eval, so you cannot tell if effort helped
flips: Latency budget moves from a few hundred milliseconds to minutes: reasoning becomes affordable
A verifier appears (tests, a checker): escalate effort only on failures instead of paying everywhere
You swap models: re-check supported effort values and defaults, because some reject `none` or `budget_tokens`

pitfalls.symptom: Response is `incomplete` with no visible answer
pitfalls.cause: The output cap was spent on reasoning tokens
pitfalls.fix: Reserve at least 25,000 tokens when starting, tune from measured reasoning tokens and alert on `incomplete` with reason `max_output_tokens`.

pitfalls.cause: The new model rejects an effort value (`none`) or manual `budget_tokens`
pitfalls.fix: Keep a per-model capability table and a contract test that sends your real settings to each candidate model.

scenarios.title: Voice assistant, routine intents
scenarios.situation: A voice assistant answers account and policy lookups. Users notice any pause. Almost every request is a routine intent, and a few are ambiguous.
constraints: Time to first audio must stay under about a second
Tasks are routine lookups with known answers
Volume is high and cost per call matters
unknowns: What share of requests fail on a standard model?
Is there a cheaper path to handle the ambiguous few?
scenarios.question: How do you configure thinking?

options.name: Reasoning model at default effort for everything
options.why: Every call pays hidden tokens and delay for tasks a standard model already solves.
options.tradeoff: Right for a background analysis path where latency is relaxed and failures are costly.

options.name: Standard model or the lowest supported effort
options.why: The tasks are routine, so extra thinking adds latency and output cost without a measurable gain.
options.tradeoff: Hard ambiguous requests may fail. Route those to a slower path.

options.name: High effort only when a classifier flags ambiguity
options.why: Matches effort to difficulty and protects the fast path.
options.tradeoff: Adds a classifier and an extra latency path to build and evaluate.

flips.if: The assistant becomes a chat helper with a 30-second budget
flips.then: A reasoning model at default effort becomes reasonable if evals show gains.
Use its lowest supported effort or a non-reasoning model, and add a contract test.

scenarios.takeaway: Latency-bound routine work should not pay for hidden thinking.

scenarios.title: Overnight migration with tests
scenarios.situation: A batch job rewrites thousands of code files to a new library. Each file has unit tests. The job runs overnight and spend is reviewed weekly.
constraints: Budget is limited but failures are expensive to fix by hand
unknowns: What is the pass rate at default effort?
How many failures pass at the next effort level?
scenarios.question: How do you spend thinking?

options.name: Max effort on every file
options.why: Simple and gives the best chance per file.
options.tradeoff: Pays top price on the many files that default effort already passes.

options.name: Low effort plus a long scripted step-by-step prompt
options.why: OpenAI advises goals, constraints and an output contract for reasoning models, and scripted steps replace measured effort with guesswork.
options.tradeoff: Scripted steps can suit a standard model that has no reasoning control.

options.name: Default effort first, retry failures at higher effort
options.why: Tests act as a verifier, so you pay for extra thinking only on the files that need it.
options.tradeoff: Needs retry logic and a cap on attempts per file.

flips.then: You cannot escalate on failure. Run an eval sample first to pick one fixed effort.

flips.if: Failures at default effort are rare
flips.then: Keep default effort and skip the retry tier.

scenarios.takeaway: A verifier lets you buy effort only where it pays.

scenarios.title: Tool loop under zero data retention
scenarios.situation: An agent calls functions in a loop on a new reasoning model. The organization is approved for zero data retention, so nothing may be stored server side.
constraints: Quality in multi-step tool use must hold
unknowns: Does the model support function calling on Chat Completions?
Which effort values does it accept?
scenarios.question: How do you build the loop?

options.name: Responses API, stateless, passing reasoning items back
options.why: Reasoning items carry `encrypted_content` in stateless mode, so continuity survives without server-side storage.
options.tradeoff: Your code carries the items and the larger payload.

options.name: Chat Completions with function tools
options.why: GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol do not support function calling on Chat Completions.
options.tradeoff: Fine on older models that support it and where you do not need reasoning continuity.

options.name: Responses API but drop reasoning items from each turn
options.why: OpenAI recommends passing back reasoning items with function outputs, so dropping them breaks the documented path.
options.tradeoff: Acceptable only if an eval shows no quality loss and you need to cut payload size.

flips.if: ZDR does not apply and server-side state is allowed
flips.then: Use `previous_response_id` and let the service carry reasoning state.

flips.if: The model supports function calling on Chat Completions
flips.then: Chat Completions is possible, but you still need to return reasoning state yourself.

scenarios.takeaway: Stateless reasoning loops need the Responses API and returned reasoning items.

quiz.q: A reasoning request returns `status: incomplete` and no visible text. What is the most likely cause?
options: The model refused the request and returned an empty message
The prompt cache expired between turns
The effort was set too low
quiz.explain: Reasoning tokens count against the output cap, so a cap that is too low can end the response before any visible text. A refusal returns text, cache expiry only changes cost and a low effort would use fewer reasoning tokens.

quiz.q: Which statements about reasoning controls are true?
options: Effort values and defaults are model-specific
Manual `budget_tokens` returns HTTP 400 on Claude 4.7 and later
Effort only changes answer quality, not cost
quiz.explain: Values and defaults differ per model, and Claude 4.7 and later reject `budget_tokens`. GPT-6 Astra rejects `none` with HTTP 400. Effort changes hidden token use, so it changes cost and latency too.

quiz.q: Which change most justifies raising effort on a task?
options: An eval showing a gain at the higher level
A larger context window on the same model family
A new vendor SDK release with a changelog
A request to sound more careful in answers
quiz.explain: Effort is a cost and latency dial, so raise it when measured results improve. Window size, SDK versions and tone requests are not evidence that more thinking helps.
